project.name: docker-zero
project.summary: A stand-in for Docker used in tests: programs that drive Docker talk to it as if it were real, but no containers run. It imitates containers, networks, ports, Nginx and Redis, and can fail on purpose so failure handling can be tested quickly.

nodes.label: Program start

nodes.label: Docker requests
nodes.summary: Answers the requests Docker tools send, for containers, images, networks and volumes, the way Docker would.

nodes.label: Pretend engine
nodes.summary: Keeps the state of every pretend container, network, address and port, and records every call in order.

nodes.label: Pretend Nginx and Redis
nodes.summary: Makes pretend web servers and Redis databases answer like the real ones, including copies that follow a main one.

nodes.label: Scenarios

s: The real HTTP client also verifies that headers are flushed before waiting: Docker SDK callers must be able to subscribe before starting a container.
Restarting a stopped container starts a new process; it does not constitute the next exit for an observer subscribed after the previous process stopped.

flows.title: A test starts services with Docker Compose

steps.note: The test runs Docker Compose pointed at the stand-in.
The stand-in answers the create and start requests exactly as Docker would.
It gives each pretend container an address and ports and records every step.
The chosen scenario decides whether each service comes up healthy or fails.
Pretend Nginx and Redis answer the test's own requests.
